transcript: Yesterday, Paul and I went to see Yellow Face on Broadway. The is a satirical, semi-autobiographical play by David Henry Hwang about a playwright, Hwang himself, leading an important conversation about Asian representation in the arts but then finding himself entangled in a controversial casting situation. From there, the play kind of expands more into a thesis on identity and the arts, politics, and the Asian American experience woven through different plot points of the playwright navigating his career, his relationship with his father, and his relationship with media and American society in general. There’s a lot baked into this play, but rest assured it is plot driven and it's a comedy. Grounded in great performances by an ensemble led by a wonderful Daniel Dae Kim, this play is funny, pointed, unapologetic — describeable in a lot of ways that I feel are quite subversive to Asian stereotypes. And I love subversion. With that, another playbill for my collection.
